codes.meaning: device qualification adapter returned an output of the wrong kind
codes.justification: Device qualification runs on real GPU hardware outside checked Invar source; an adapter whose output type differs from its case is refused.

codes.meaning: device qualification corpus contains a duplicate invocation id
codes.justification: The bounded device corpus is assembled from family generators, not from checked source; a repeated invocation id is refused.

codes.meaning: device qualification corpus exceeds its case bound
codes.justification: The bounded device corpus is assembled from family generators, not from checked source; a corpus above its case bound is refused.

codes.meaning: device completion was not confirmed
codes.justification: Device qualification runs on real GPU hardware outside checked Invar source; unconfirmed completion is reported, never counted as a pass.

codes.meaning: device output words differ from the independent expectation
codes.justification: Device qualification runs on real GPU hardware outside checked Invar source; any word that differs from the independent expectation fails the row.

codes.meaning: the requested qualification target needs its Cargo feature and host
codes.justification: Device qualification runs on real GPU hardware outside checked Invar source; a binary built without the cuda or metal feature, or on another host, refuses the target.

codes.meaning: device qualification input exceeds a device limit
codes.justification: Device qualification runs on real GPU hardware outside checked Invar source; inputs above the device admission limits are refused.

codes.meaning: device kernel launch failed
codes.justification: Device qualification runs on real GPU hardware outside checked Invar source; a failed launch is reported as such.

codes.meaning: the device rows were not requested in this CPU qualification run
codes.justification: A CPU-only qualification run records every device row as unavailable by request; this is an environment outcome, not source behaviour.

codes.meaning: device allocation failed
codes.justification: Device qualification runs on real GPU hardware outside checked Invar source; device memory exhaustion is reported, never retried on the CPU as a pass.

codes.meaning: device path refused the work
codes.justification: Device qualification runs on real GPU hardware outside checked Invar source; a typed device refusal is reported per row.

codes.meaning: device toolchain failed or mismatched
codes.justification: Device qualification runs on real GPU hardware outside checked Invar source; a device compiler or library mismatch is reported per row.

codes.meaning: no usable qualification device could be opened
codes.justification: Device qualification runs on real GPU hardware outside checked Invar source; a host without the GPU refuses the target.

codes.meaning: the strict f32 CPU oracle refused a device case
codes.justification: The strict f32 oracle evaluates generated device cases outside checked source; a case it refuses cannot be qualified.

codes.meaning: bounded adapters cannot close the frozen-shape prerequisites
codes.justification: Device qualification is bounded; criterion (c) and the frozen shapes stay pending until the M5-01 freeze, outside any source program.

codes.meaning: a GPU-required qualification report has rows without device execution
codes.justification: The --require-gpu gate is an environment outcome: rows that did not execute on the requested device fail it.

codes.meaning: a case's independent expectation could not be computed
codes.justification: Independent expectations are computed by host code outside checked source; a case without one is refused.

codes.meaning: the interaction-net encoding or verification of a qualified program failed
codes.justification: The harness encodes only programs that already passed the checker and MIR verifier, so a failing encoding is a harness or engine defect.

codes.meaning: a refusal carries a span outside the refused input
codes.justification: The front end bounds every refusal span by the input it refused; a span past the input end or reversed is a front-end defect the fuzz denominator would expose.

codes.meaning: a library baseline output differs from its reference
codes.justification: Device qualification runs on real GPU hardware outside checked Invar source; a library fixture whose full output is not exact fails its row.

codes.meaning: no library baseline exists for this family on this target
codes.justification: Library baselines are external fixtures; a family with no fixture API on a target is recorded as unavailable.

codes.meaning: the library baseline's numeric policy is not yet ruled
codes.justification: Library baselines are external fixtures; a matrix baseline awaiting its numeric policy ruling is recorded as pending.

codes.meaning: a library baseline fixture was refused by its runner
codes.justification: Device qualification runs on real GPU hardware outside checked Invar source; a fixture refused by the family baseline runner fails its row.

codes.meaning: no library fixture directory was supplied
codes.justification: Library baselines are external fixtures; without an absolute fixture directory the library rows stay pending.

codes.meaning: matrix device case could not be prepared or emitted
codes.justification: Device qualification runs on real GPU hardware outside checked Invar source; a matrix contract that cannot be emitted for the device fails its row.

codes.meaning: a device path accepted input it must refuse
codes.justification: Device qualification runs on real GPU hardware outside checked Invar source; a device path that accepts a deliberately invalid input fails the boundary check.

codes.meaning: a mutation control could not build its unmutated baseline
codes.justification: Mutation controls start from fixed valid programs that always encode and verify; a baseline that fails to build is a harness defect.

codes.meaning: a deliberate wrong-result mutation was not detected
codes.justification: Mutation controls run inside the qualification harness, outside checked source; a surviving mutation fails the harness.

codes.meaning: the native engine failed to compile or run a qualified program
codes.justification: The native engine runs only MIR that already verified and agreed with the reference; a build, link or host failure is an engine defect.

codes.meaning: the executable-net lowering or verification of a qualified program failed
codes.justification: The harness lowers only programs that already passed the checker, so a net that fails to lower, verify or compile is an engine defect.

codes.meaning: the net oracle refused a verified candidate
codes.justification: The oracle runs only the net and proof the harness just verified, so a refusal means a stale or mismatched proof, an engine defect.

codes.meaning: the CUDA target needs an absolute NVRTC helper path
codes.justification: Device qualification runs on real GPU hardware outside checked Invar source; CUDA qualification refuses to run without an absolute existing NVRTC helper.

codes.meaning: the device is not the pinned qualification target
codes.justification: Device qualification runs on real GPU hardware outside checked Invar source; any device other than the pinned target is refused before any work.

codes.meaning: unconfirmed device work was not quarantined
codes.justification: Device qualification runs on real GPU hardware outside checked Invar source; the quarantine check fails a row whose unconfirmed work escaped quarantine.

codes.meaning: a qualification report is missing required rows or fields
codes.justification: Qualification reports are harness documents, not source output; an incomplete report is refused.

codes.meaning: a qualification report could not be written without replacing an existing one
codes.justification: Report publication touches the host filesystem; a missing directory, a full disk or an existing report is refused and never overwritten.

codes.meaning: a qualification report exceeds its 4 MiB bound
codes.justification: Reports are harness documents bounded by the publisher, not by checked source; an oversized report is refused before any file is created.

codes.meaning: two engines disagree on a program's observable semantics
codes.justification: Every engine must reproduce the reference observation exactly; a disagreement is an engine defect, never a property of the source program.

codes.meaning: the source program has no device-eligible region
codes.justification: Device qualification runs on real GPU hardware outside checked Invar source; a source case with no device-eligible region is reported as ineligible, not as a pass.

codes.meaning: stencil device case could not be prepared
codes.justification: Device qualification runs on real GPU hardware outside checked Invar source; a stencil contract outside its device bounds fails its row.

codes.meaning: a strict f32 device case fell back to the CPU for subnormal handling
codes.justification: Device qualification runs on real GPU hardware outside checked Invar source; a device that must hand subnormal work back to the CPU records that row as a fallback, never as a device pass.

codes.meaning: bounded summary device case could not be prepared
codes.justification: Device qualification runs on real GPU hardware outside checked Invar source; a bounded summary contract that cannot run on the device fails its row.

codes.meaning: the target's device rows were not executed
codes.justification: Device rows are recorded as not executed when no hardware run was requested; this is an environment outcome, not source behaviour.

codes.meaning: Tensor Core output exceeds its error bound
codes.justification: Device qualification runs on real GPU hardware outside checked Invar source; a tc-f16-f32-v1 result outside the amended D5 bound fails its row.

codes.meaning: the front end refused a corpus program the corpus did not expect to be refused
codes.justification: Corpus programs state their expected outcome; an unexpected refusal means the corpus and the front end disagree, a harness defect.

codes.meaning: a refusal lacks a code or a source span
codes.justification: The front end gives every refusal a code and every source error a span; an untyped refusal is a front-end defect the fuzz denominator would expose.

codes.meaning: the native qualification rows need a binary built with the native feature
codes.justification: A qualification binary built without the native feature records the native rows as unavailable; this is a build outcome, not source behaviour.
